text:
Power Stations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document lists the equipment inspection I1, 
to be performed every six months as indicated by M6 in the above title 
block.
This first draft is initiated by eng. Samy Mohamed Hassan, tested by tested by 
Hassan Ahmed Mohamed Rostm, at 14 Jan 2004, revised by EDEPCo. quality 
control eng. Tawfeq El-abasey, accepted 
by general manager eng. Mohamed Abd El Ghaffar, and certified by eng. Moustafa 
Al Lethy; EDEPCo. Inspection & QC head sector.
Technical Data:
 Main supply (3 
phases) 380VAC 10% voltage
Frequency 50 HZ 
5%
Battery charge 
data:
 Boost charge 
current 26A
 Voltage 
variation during the boost charge 123V 146V
 Trickle 
charge voltage 124V 2%
 Max voltage 
in manual charge 154V
Load supply data:
 Current 
 60 A
 Voltage 
 110 10%
 Ripple (with 
battery) 5% Vn
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and the qualified
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the
work area.
Wear your safety helmet, shoes and safety clothes when cleaning.
Isolate the rectifier/charger out of service and earth.
The presence of current in load is signaled by flashing caution lamp and a 
 display segment.
Tools and
Equipment
Safety 
 helmet, shoes,
Screw driver set,
 Air blower
Fine cloth for cleaning purposes.
Portable earth discharging test loads
Visual Checks and General 
Cleaning
Through cleaning of all power semi conductors and of all control P.C. 
 boards, remove foreign matter, if any.
Check of tightness of all electrical and mechanical connections.
Check that all P.C. boards are correctly plugged in their seats and that 
 electromechanical components are well seated on their bases.
Check that all vents be clean "remove possible digging material"
Check that there is no condensate build up or water seepage.
Check of the batteries.
Operational Checks
Check that all signals and instruments furnish the correct indication.
Check the correct operation of the system and/or equipment in the correct 
 entirely.
Check the setting value.
If there are any failures in the equipment, check that all input and output 
 voltages do correspond to the equipment plate rating, then, check possible 
 alarm indication on the board front.
Check that there is no condensate build up or water seepage.
Checkout of the batteries.
